Posted September 24, 2004
Analysis by Richard Cowan Sponsored by Advanced Nutrients.

Michael Kinsley once said, A gaffe is when a politician tells the truth. When John Walters tells the truth it might better be called a miracle, but then even then he has to give it a bodyguard of lies .
See
 The Myth That The Washington Post and John Walters Are Harmless; Drug Czar Puts Hyperlying About Cannabis At The Center of the War on Freedom.

Yesterday, the Chicago Sun Times reported that Walters would neither support or oppose a proposal by a Chicago Police Sergeant subsequently endorsed by the city's politically powerful Mayor Daley that would allow the city to fine people with less than an ounce of cannabis, rather than charging them with a misdemeanor under Illinois state law. (A number of cities, especially college towns, in DEAland have similar policies. Twelve states have some form of decriminalization.)

This is the same John Walters that warned Canada that, if it passed a similar law, DEAland would make life very difficult for Canadians trying to cross the world's longest undefended border.
See
 John Walters Testimony To The Canadian Parliament. The Public Record Or What He Would Have Said, If He Was Not Afraid of Being Asked Embarrassing Questions. The Battle for Canada.
and
 As Canada Moves Toward Some Form Of Decriminalization, Canadian Narks and Walters Escalate Lying. The New Math. Canada Replaces Mexico As Leading Supplier of Cannabis. And If You Believe That

Of course, after a year or two of reporting Czarist threats, the Canadian media and politicians finally discovered that some 100 million Americans live in states that decriminalized possession decades ago.

As ever, the devil is in the details. Is the Czar is going soft, or is he just recognizing reality? Alternatively, in keeping with Kinsley's dictum, maybe he was just drunk.

The Sun Times article reports:

It's clear from the high dismissal rate of marijuana-possession cases in Chicago that authorities are not treating pot as seriously as they should, said John Walters, the White House's top drug-fighting official.

His remarks came in an interview a day after Daley embraced a Chicago Police sergeant's plan to impose fines on pot smokers ranging from $250 for up to 10 grams to $1,000 for 20 to 30 grams.

Sgt. Thomas Donegan, fed up with seeing pot arrests evaporate in court, presented top police brass with a report last week showing that 6,954 cases -- 94 percent of those involving less than 2.5 grams of pot -- were dismissed in 2003.

Donegan suggested that fines for possession of less than 30 grams of pot -- a misdemeanor -- could have raised $5 million last year.

A hearing would still be held for people fined for having pot, but the standard of proof would be lower than in a misdemeanor case, and the ticket would not go on their criminal record, making it likely that they would pay instead of fighting it, Donegan said. Police could still make arrests on a state misdemeanor drug charge, if, for example, the suspect were a repeat drug offender.

Walters did not object to the concept of imposing fines on people caught with small amounts of pot. But he would not express outright support for the idea, either.

Instead, he said fines could be a " tool " for reducing pot consumption, along with opening up more drug courts and requiring pot smokers to attend classes to learn about the dangers of the drug.

Walters, however, did not echo fears by some in law enforcement that imposing fines for pot would show that the city is not serious about pot consumption.

" Some people will read that fines downgrade our concern about the issue, " he said. " I don't read that. "

He stressed that the goal of enforcing laws on marijuana possession should not be locking up the offenders, but educating them that pot has become more potent in the last 10 years and that more users are winding up in hospitals.
See

Walters said 4,588 people visited emergency rooms in the Chicago area in 2002 because of pot-related problems and 4,800 people were admitted to substance-abuse programs in 2001 for marijuana treatment.
See
 Cannabis Prohibition Prostitutes Science In New Emergency Dept. Data. Hiding the Truth Behind A Cloud of Lies.
and
 Walters Tells a New Lie. Oh Happy Day! People Need Treatment If They Are Sent to Treatment, By Definition. And How Do They Treat Marijuana Addicts? We Couldn't Make This Up, But They Did.

Scientific improvements in the cultivation of marijuana have increased the content of the active ingredient -- THC -- from about 1 percent to 2 percent of the total weight to an average of 9 percent, Walters said.
See
 European Study Shows Potency of Prohibitionist Propaganda. CBS and The AP Lie to the American People About the Dutch. Surprise!

" I certainly agree with the frustration reflected in the comments by the mayor and law enforcement in Chicago, " Walters said.

" There is an unwillingness now in most jurisdictions to take seriously enough the problem of marijuana trafficking and consumption. "

From the Sun Times in 2001 see
 Ottawa Citizen's Dan Gardner Says " U.S. Bullies World Into Waging Futile Drug War " --UK Article Demonstrates How This Continues.

It is unfortunate that the Sun Times did not offer its readers any of the government's own data that would have shown that the Czar was lying, as usual.
See
 Bush Should Have John Comical Ali Walters Explain The Iraq War, Then The Media Would Never Ask Any Embarrassing Questions. Doctrine Of Drug Czar Infallibility? Blame Canada, Again.

However, Canadians should wonder how it is that they are expected to treat their citizens much more harshly than our Lord and Master, the Czar, would impose on his American subjects.

The problem for the Canadian prohibitionists is that they are incapable of independent thinking. This is going to ever so terribly confusing to them. They can no longer fall back on the phony realism that Canada cannot decriminalize possession because the US won't let them.

Also, they will have a hard time with the fact that the Chicago proposal sets a 30 gram limit, while the Martin government's bill would only decriminalize 15 grams. That will shatter the conceit so beloved of Canadian liberals that they are daringly progressive and far ahead of the US on everything good and noble. Never mind the fact that Ohio decriminalized 100 grams in the 1970s.

Of course, the high fines will just be one more example of the middle class exemption from the marijuana laws. The young, the poor, and medical users in particular, will be badly hurt by $1,000 fines. Presumably those who cannot pay will be sent to jail. That was the experience in South Australia.
See
 The Patriot Act Hits A New Low As The Prison/Probation/Parole Population Hits A New High.
and links

In the meantime, well below everyone's radar, Alaska may legalize the cultivation, sale and possession of cannabis this November.
See http://www.yeson2alaska.com/

The state's Supreme Court has already legalized possession in the home of up to four ounces.
See
Justices Uphold Right To Use Pot

The Canadian Parliament is unlikely to do anything with the pending bill until well after the DEAland elections. By then events in Alaska and Chicago may make the Martin bill look like the absurd fraud that it really is.
